title: China-to-Germany Industrial Motor Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: IE efficiency class scope for Germany
rows.target_requirement: Industrial AC motors placed on the German market within the 0.75-1000 kW EU ErP scope must meet the applicable IE efficiency class under EU Regulation 2019/1781. Germany applies the EU rule directly, with BNetzA market surveillance. The core threshold is IE3 for 0.75-1000 kW motors since July 2021, with a stricter IE4 tier for motors at and above 75 kW since July 2023 where the Regulation applies.
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 18613 for IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC 60034-30-1 naming, with GB 12665 for cooling-related baseline considerations and CCC as a baseline only for low-voltage motors in CCC scope. These China-side baselines do not create Germany or EU market approval.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The China IE label or GB 18613 evidence must be mapped to the EU ErP legal threshold before German market placement. The German target column is not satisfied by CCC or by a China-only IE declaration because BNetzA can request EU-format evidence against Regulation 2019/1781.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory in Germany under directly applicable EU Regulation 2019/1781
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or baseline depending on product scope under GB 18613 and CCC catalogue status

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat Germany as an EU ErP market with active surveillance. A China IE3 or CCC file is not enough unless the motor is documented against EU Regulation 2019/1781 and the applicable IE3 or IE4 threshold.

rows.target_requirement: Germany uses a 400/230 V, three-phase, 50 Hz supply convention. The 50 Hz frequency aligns with China, but the common German three-phase nominal voltage is 400 V rather than China's 380 V. Rated performance, nameplate data, temperature rise, and efficiency claims should be checked at the intended German supply conditions.
target_standards: Germany 400/230 V three-phase 50 Hz grid convention
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly rates three-phase industrial motors for 380 V, 50 Hz. GB 18613 efficiency evidence, GB 12665 cooling assumptions, and CCC baseline documentation may therefore reflect Chinese nominal voltage conditions rather than the German 400 V system.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The shared 50 Hz frequency reduces redesign burden, but 380 V China ratings should not be treated as automatically equivalent to 400 V Germany ratings. Export documentation should confirm 400 V operation, nameplate marking, and any efficiency declaration used for CE and ErP evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory as part of truthful rating, CE technical documentation, and German market placement evidence
mandatory_status.cn: Baseline technical rating under China GB and CCC documentation where applicable

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A 380 V, 50 Hz China motor may be close to German operating conditions, but the Germany file should explicitly support 400 V, 50 Hz use and should not rely on China voltage assumptions alone.

rows.target_requirement: For Germany, EU Regulation 2019/1781 sets the mandatory minimum energy efficiency requirement for industrial AC motors in the 0.75-1000 kW scope. Since July 2021, IE3 has been the mandatory minimum for that scope where the Regulation applies. The requirement is enforced through EU and German market surveillance, including BNetzA activity in Germany.
rows.china_equivalent: China's common equivalent is GB 18613 for motor IE efficiency classes, aligned in structure with IEC 60034-30-1. GB 12665 and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope may be part of the China compliance baseline, but they are not German market-entry approvals.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: Even when the China file says IE3 under GB 18613, the German importer needs EU ErP evidence and technical documentation suitable for Regulation 2019/1781. CCC is not recognized as proof of EU ErP compliance.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — IE3 minimum in Germany for applicable 0.75-1000 kW motors since July 2021
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory baseline under GB 18613 where the motor is in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Germany, IE3 is a legal ErP floor for applicable 0.75-1000 kW motors, not a voluntary marketing claim. China GB or CCC evidence must be converted into an EU Regulation 2019/1781 compliance file.

rows.requirement: IE4 tier for 75 kW and above
rows.target_requirement: From July 2023, EU Regulation 2019/1781 introduced a stricter IE4 requirement for motors at and above 75 kW where the Regulation applies. For Germany, this tier is strictly enforced before placing the motor on the market. An IE3-only motor in this power range should be treated as a high-risk non-compliance unless the exact regulatory scope confirms an exemption.
rows.china_equivalent: GB 18613 includes IE efficiency classes aligned with IEC naming, so China-side IE4 evidence may exist for higher efficiency products. However, many China baseline files may only demonstrate IE3, plus GB 12665 and CCC where applicable, which is not enough for the German IE4 tier.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The main Germany gap is the post-July 2023 IE4 tier. A China motor that is acceptable domestically at IE3 can still fail German market placement if it falls into the 75 kW and above EU ErP IE4 scope.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — IE4 for applicable motors at and above 75 kW since July 2023
mandatory_status.cn: IE4 may be available under GB 18613 classing but is not a substitute for Germany evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Germany-facing 75 kW and above motors should be screened first for the IE4 tier. IE3-only China documentation is a likely blocker for German market access where EU Regulation 2019/1781 applies.

rows.target_requirement: For German market placement, declared motor efficiency must be backed by an EU-compliant technical file and product information suitable for CE and ErP scrutiny. The file should support the declared IE class, rated voltage and frequency, and the efficiency values used in the Declaration of Conformity and product information.
rows.china_equivalent: China files commonly include GB 18613 efficiency class evidence, GB 12665 cooling-related evidence, and CCC where the less than 1 kV motor is in CCC scope. These files may not contain the same EU-format declared values or DoC references required for Germany.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The Germany gap is often documentation rather than only motor hardware. The exporter must provide EU-ready efficiency evidence and product information, not only China test reports or a CCC certificate.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — EU technical documentation and product information must support German market placement
mandatory_status.cn: China evidence is baseline only and must be mapped before export

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build the Germany file around EU ErP declared values and CE documentation. China GB 18613 and CCC evidence may support engineering review but does not replace the EU technical file.

rows.target_requirement: For Germany, EMC Directive 2014/30/EU applies where an industrial motor or motor package is apparatus capable of generating or being affected by electromagnetic disturbance, especially where drives, controls, or electronics are supplied with the motor. CE marking and an EU Declaration of Conformity must cover EMC where applicable before placing the product on the German market.
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline files for motors may focus on GB 18613 efficiency, GB 12665 cooling, and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope. These do not automatically provide EU EMC evidence for Germany.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: A China motor package sold with electronics can require EMC conformity for Germany even if the China file has no equivalent mandatory EMC step. The German target file should define the product boundary and include EMC evidence where the Directive applies.

mandatory_status.cn: Not established by the China motor efficiency and CCC baseline alone

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Germany, identify whether the supplied motor is a bare motor or an electronic motor package. If EMC applies, CE and DoC must include EMC Directive 2014/30/EU; CCC is not recognized as a substitute.

rows.requirement: EMC evidence for drives and controls
rows.target_requirement: When an industrial motor is supplied with a variable speed drive, inverter, soft starter, controller, or similar electronics for Germany, the conformity assessment should cover the electromagnetic environment and system configuration. The CE technical file should support emission and immunity claims and the EU DoC should list the applicable EMC law.
rows.china_equivalent: China-side motor documentation commonly anchors on GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope. Those files may not contain system-level drive EMC test evidence needed for a German CE file.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The German gap is system boundary discipline. A compliant motor alone does not automatically make the motor-plus-drive package EMC compliant, and a China CCC or GB file may not address the final configuration.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for applicable electronic motor systems placed on the German market
mandatory_status.cn: China baseline does not replace EU EMC conformity

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] German CE review should test the actual motor-drive configuration, not only the bare motor. EMC evidence should match the supplied system boundary and intended industrial environment.

rows.requirement: CE marking and EU Declaration of Conformity before Germany placement
rows.target_requirement: Before an industrial motor is placed on the German market, CE marking and an EU Declaration of Conformity are required for applicable EU laws, including Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU, EMC Directive 2014/30/EU where applicable, and EU Regulation 2019/1781 for Ecodesign efficiency. The DoC and technical file must be available for market surveillance.
rows.china_equivalent: China-side evidence may include GB 18613 efficiency documents, GB 12665 cooling documents, and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope. These are domestic or China-export baselines and are not recognized as CE marking or an EU Declaration of Conformity.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The Germany market-entry gap is formal EU conformity, not only technical similarity. CE marking must be backed by a DoC and technical file before import or first making available in Germany.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory before placing on the German market
mandatory_status.cn: China standards and CCC are not CE or EU DoC substitutes

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not ship to Germany on CCC or GB evidence alone. CE marking, an EU Declaration of Conformity, and a supporting technical file are the core market-entry package.

rows.requirement: EU authorised representative or responsible economic operator
rows.target_requirement: Non-EU manufacturers exporting industrial motors to Germany need an EU-based authorised representative or another responsible economic operator in the EU supply chain where required by EU market surveillance rules. The responsible party must be able to provide the DoC and technical documentation to authorities.
rows.china_equivalent: China does not provide an equivalent outbound authorised representative system for Germany. GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC records do not create an EU legal representative or responsible economic operator.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: This is a legal-supply-chain gap. A technically compliant motor can still be blocked or withdrawn in Germany if no EU responsible party can provide the required file.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where EU market surveillance rules require an EU responsible economic operator
mandatory_status.cn: No direct China equivalent for Germany market responsibility

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Germany exports by non-EU manufacturers should assign and document the EU responsible party before shipment. This is separate from GB, CCC, or efficiency testing.

rows.target_requirement: Germany enforces EU product compliance through national market surveillance. For industrial motors, BNetzA can be relevant for market surveillance, while DGUV and VDE technical standards may shape safety expectations. Authorities may request the EU DoC, technical file, efficiency evidence, labels, and supply-chain responsible party details.
rows.china_equivalent: China-side GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC records may support domestic regulatory review but are not designed for German BNetzA document requests or EU-format surveillance files.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The German enforcement gap is readiness. A supplier should be able to respond quickly with EU-format CE, DoC, ErP, LVD, EMC, label, and representative documents, not translate China-only certificates after the fact.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory to cooperate with German and EU market surveillance
mandatory_status.cn: China documents may be supporting inputs only

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Germany, assume BNetzA or another authority may ask for an EU-format file. Build the file before shipment and do not rely on CCC recognition, because CCC is not recognized for German market approval.

rows.target_requirement: Industrial AC motors placed on the German market must meet Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU where the voltage scope applies. The CE file should address electrical safety, insulation, temperature rise, mechanical risks connected with electrical safety, labels, instructions, and a Declaration of Conformity before placing on the market.
rows.china_equivalent: China-side motor safety and performance evidence commonly sits with GB 18613 for efficiency, GB 12665 for cooling-related baseline, and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope. Those records may support engineering review but are not the German LVD legal file.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: Germany requires an EU LVD conformity position. A China safety or CCC baseline does not by itself create CE marking, an EU DoC, German-language instructions, or an EU technical file.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU applies
mandatory_status.cn: China safety and CCC evidence is baseline only

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Germany, prepare an LVD-backed CE file even if the motor already has China safety or CCC evidence. The legal package must be EU-format and available before market placement.

rows.target_requirement: German industrial buyers, installers, and safety reviewers often expect DGUV-compatible workplace safety documentation and VDE-aligned electrical technical evidence, even when the legal market-entry basis is EU CE law. Instructions, warnings, labels, and installation information should be suitable for German industrial use.
rows.china_equivalent: China documentation under GB 18613, GB 12665, and CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope may not contain Germany-facing workplace safety language, VDE-style installation expectations, or EU CE risk documentation.
china_standards: CCC for less than 1 kV motors in CCC scope
rows.gap: The commercial and safety acceptance gap in Germany includes language, installation, and workplace documentation. A China technical certificate can be insufficient for German users even where the hardware is similar.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory or buyer-required depending on legal scope, installation context, and German workplace safety expectations
mandatory_status.cn: Not covered by China baseline documents alone

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Germany, align the safety file, instructions, and installation evidence with EU CE law plus German DGUV/VDE expectations. Do not treat China certificates as sufficient user-facing safety documentation.
